title: Air-fryer tandoori chicken
subtitle: Deeply spiced chicken with yoghurt marinade, charred in the air fryer.
excerpt: Chicken pieces in a tandoori-spiced yoghurt marinade, air-fried at high heat for charred edges and red-tinged skin. Bolder in spice than tikka, with the same high-heat cooking method. Serves four.
sourceNotes: Tandoori chicken originated in what is now the Punjab region and spread through Indian restaurant cooking worldwide. The distinctive red colour traditionally comes from Kashmiri chilli powder. This air-fryer version uses bone-in thighs and drumsticks, which stay moist at high heat.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze marinated raw chicken for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge overnight.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch easily. Cook in two rounds in the air fryer.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate for up to 24 hours in the fridge.

content.text: Tandoori chicken is the chicken tikka's bone-in relation: larger pieces, more spice, longer cooking. The marinade is similar but bolder, and the cooking time is longer because bone-in pieces take more time to cook through. Slash the skin before marinating so the spice paste reaches the meat.

items.prepNote: bone-in, skin-on, slashed 3 times to the bone

content.text: Combine {{plain-yoghurt}} of yoghurt, {{lemon-juice}} of lemon juice, {{garlic}} of grated garlic, and {{ginger-root}} of ginger in a bowl. Add {{garam-masala}} of garam masala, {{cumin-ground}} of cumin, {{paprika-hot}} of hot paprika, {{turmeric}} of turmeric, and {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt. Stir well. Slash the skin on the {{chicken-thigh}} thighs and {{chicken-drumsticks}} drumsticks. Rub the marinade deep into the cuts. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.

Preheat the air fryer to 220°C. Shake excess marinade from the pieces and place in a single layer. Spray with cooking oil. Cook for 13 minutes, flip, and cook for a further 10-12 minutes until charred at the edges and the juices run clear. Check that the thickest part of the thigh reads 75°C.

items.fix: Slash the skin and flesh before marinating. The marinade penetrates the cuts and the slashes also help heat reach the bone.
Empty the drip tray halfway through cooking. A small amount of smoke is expected at 220°C.

items.cause: Temperature not high enough, or too much marinade left on.
items.fix: Shake off the excess before cooking. The fryer must be fully preheated.

items.symptom: Dry thigh meat near the bone
items.fix: Pull at 75°C. Bone-in thighs hold moisture well, but overcooking past 80°C dries them out.

content.text: Tandoori chicken is a centrepiece dish: serve it with naan, rice, sliced onion and lemon wedges, raita on the side. The same marinade works on a whole spatchcocked chicken, which then needs about 35 minutes in the air fryer.
